Simulation: One Latent Ordering

Ziang Zhang

Question and design

Can a single MPCurve ordering recover a known sample trajectory from noisy two-dimensional observations? We use the spiral generator from the MPCurver getting-started article: 1,000 samples with latent \(t\in[1.5\pi,4.5\pi]\) and Gaussian noise standard deviation 0.12. The simulation seed is 1. A CAVI fit uses Fiedler initialization, \(K=60\) grid positions, and at most 120 iterations.

Ordering recovery

Figure 1. The simulated spiral coloured by the generating position (left) and the inferred posterior-mean grid position (right).

The absolute Spearman correlation between true \(t\) and inferred posterior-mean grid position is 0.9998. The absolute value accounts for the arbitrary direction of an inferred ordering. This result comes from one simulated data set.

Objective trace

Figure 2. Evidence lower bound recorded during the single-ordering CAVI fit.

The ELBO increases through the fit and levels off as CAVI converges.

Reproduce

The experiment script regenerates the data, fit, and figures with MPCurver 0.3.0. The saved results include the generating truth and fitted model.
